spec.description: Host CPU saturation, Go runtime attribution, WebSocket traffic, work amplification, hub dispatch and connection pool pressure. Read it top to bottom: the first row says how hard the server is working, the rest say what the backend is working on.

spec.title: Host CPU Utilisation
spec.description: Host-wide CPU utilisation from node_exporter. This is the authoritative saturation signal for the server; the Go runtime CPU classes below are estimates used only for relative attribution.

spec.title: Go Runtime GC Share (estimate)
spec.description: Estimated share of Go runtime CPU attribution spent in garbage collection. Use this for relative allocation diagnostics, not as a host CPU measurement.

spec.title: Scheduling Delay (p99)
spec.description: How long a runnable goroutine waited for a processor. This rises before throughput falls and is the clearest sign that the process is CPU bound rather than slow.

spec.title: Goroutines
spec.description: Live goroutines. A number that climbs and never returns is a leak, and every one of them costs scheduler time.

spec.title: Go Runtime CPU Attribution (estimate)
spec.description: Estimated Go runtime CPU attribution by class. "user" is application code, "gc" is garbage collection, and "scavenge" is returning memory to the operating system. These values are not host CPU utilisation.

spec.title: Scheduler Pressure
spec.description: Scheduling delay quantiles alongside mutex wait. Mutex wait is measured in seconds of blocked time per second, so a value of 1 means one goroutine was blocked on a lock at all times.

spec.title: Garbage Collection
spec.description: Collection rate by trigger and the stop-the-world pause length. Forced cycles or a rising pause p99 point at allocation pressure rather than at request volume.

spec.title: Heap, Goroutines and Threads
spec.description: Heap size drives collection frequency, goroutine count drives scheduler load, and the operating system thread count grows when goroutines block in syscalls.

spec.title: EuroScope Sync Rate by Outcome
spec.description: Syncs that changed persisted state versus heartbeats that did not. EuroScope syncs at a fixed cadence, so "unchanged" is the normal majority and its rate tracks connected masters.

spec.title: Follow-up Work Scheduled by Sync
spec.description: Average follow-up work items scheduled by each sync, split by kind. This normalizes away changes in sync traffic so a rising line means each sync is amplifying more work.

spec.title: Recalculations per Unchanged Sync
spec.description: CDM recalculations scheduled per sync that changed nothing. A sync that changed no state should not need a full airport recalculation, so anything meaningfully above zero here is repeated work.

spec.title: DB Operations per Sync
spec.description: Database operations divided by syncs. This is the cheapest early warning that a sync has started touching rows it did not previously need.

spec.title: Sync Duration by Phase (p99)
spec.description: Which stage of a sync is slow. The phases sum to the total sync duration, so the tallest line is the one to profile.

spec.title: CDM Recalculations — Rate, Duration and Size
spec.description: A recalculation walks every strip at the airport, so it is the largest unit of work one message can trigger. Rate multiplied by duration is the share of a processor this path consumes.

spec.title: Time Spent Recalculating
spec.description: Seconds of recalculation per second. A value of 1 means one processor was doing nothing but CDM recalculation for the whole interval.

spec.title: Handler Load by Message Type
spec.description: Seconds of handler time consumed per second, by message type. This weights latency by call rate; series are not stacked, so each line is the actual load contributed by that message type.

spec.title: DB Operations per Message
spec.description: Average database operations performed by each handled message, split by type. This normalizes away traffic volume so a rising line means an individual message is doing more database work.

spec.title: Hub Queue Depth (p99)
spec.description: Backlog waiting in each hub dispatch queue. Both queues hold 256 messages; a p99 approaching that is a hub that can no longer keep up with its publishers.

spec.title: Hub Dispatch Duration (p99)
spec.description: Time the single-threaded dispatch loop spent fanning one message out. Everything the hub sends is serialised behind this, so it is a hard ceiling on broadcast throughput.

spec.title: Broadcast Fan-out (p99)
spec.description: Clients reached by one dispatched message. Dispatch cost scales with this, so fan-out growth explains dispatch duration growth without any code change.

spec.title: Back-pressure and Slow Consumers
spec.description: Publishes that had to wait for room in the hub queue, and clients dropped for failing to drain their own. Either one appearing means dispatch has fallen behind the work producing events.

spec.title: Inbound Message Rate by Type
spec.description: Rate of decoded client messages received by the backend, grouped by message type.

spec.title: Payload Bytes per Second by Direction and Client Type
spec.description: Serialized application payload throughput. Inbound is measured when a client payload is decoded; outbound when a payload is accepted by the writer. Framing, TLS, and compression are excluded.

spec.title: Payload Bytes per Second by Direction and Message Type
spec.description: Top message types by serialized application payload throughput in either direction.

spec.title: Total Payload Bytes by Direction
spec.description: Serialized application payload bytes transferred during the selected time range.

spec.title: Payload Size Percentiles by Direction and Message Type
spec.description: P50, P95, and P99 serialized application payload size for each inbound and outbound message type.

spec.title: Connection Pool Saturation
spec.description: Acquired connections against the pool maximum. A pool at its limit turns database latency into application queueing, which looks like a slow backend rather than a slow database.

spec.title: Pool Acquires
spec.description: Acquires against the acquires that found the pool empty and had to wait. Any sustained empty-acquire rate means queries are queueing for a connection before they even reach Postgres.

spec.title: Slow Operations and Dropped Clients
spec.description: Warnings emitted on the paths this dashboard measures. Each line carries the trace_id, so a slow recalculation can be opened directly as a trace.

spec.expr: {service_name="flightstrips-backend",deployment_environment="$env"} | label_format level=detected_level | level =~ `warn|error` |~ "CDM recalculation finished|Disconnecting slow websocket client"

spec.title: All Warnings and Errors
spec.description: Every warning and error from the backend, for correlating a CPU spike with what the process was complaining about.
